accuracy.evidence: Matched against CCSS 2.NBT.4 (compare two three-digit numbers using hundreds, tens and ones digits; record with >, =, <) and NC Y3 NPV (compare and order numbers up to 1000). Every pair worked by hand: 412 > 398, 352 > 325, 305 < 350, 98 < 120, 708 < 780, 406 < 460 < 604 < 640, 1000 > 999, 563 > 536.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented three-digit slips: bigger tens/ones digits winning over hundreds (398 vs 412), same-digit numbers treated as equal (305/350, 640/604), a zero that holds a place ignored, unaligned first-digit comparison (98 vs 120, 1000 vs 999), and the > sign turned the wrong way.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagord1k is a left-to-right scan of an H/T/O chart where the learner taps the deciding column, plus a 4-number same-digit ordering that lands on a 0-1000 line; flagcmp2d is two-digit tens/ones only, flaghund counts on, flagpvc reads four-digit values. Lab gate overlap under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: Tapping a matching column gives 'that place is the same, move right'; tapping too far right gives 'look further left, the hundreds already differ', so the learner discovers the scan rule before the text restates it; the order step shows the sorted set on the number line.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then disproves: '398, its digits are bigger', 'Equal: same digits' for 352/325 and 305/350, '98, because 9 > 1', and 604 as smallest of 640/604/460/406.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge pairs, each wrong symbol tagged: ones (smaller places allowed to win), zero (a zero holding a place ignored), lead (unaligned first digits), flip (sign reversed), same (same digits taken as equal), each with its own message naming that slip.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and Year 3 terms (hundreds, tens, ones, greater, less, place); family kid FK under the 5.0 target in validate_lessons; adult text names the standard, the scan method and five mistakes.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate clean of filler; each kid paragraph adds one rule (places, hundreds first, move right on a match, zero holds a place, align a two-digit number) and each lab step teaches one of them.

mobile.evidence: Tall 1.2 canvas at 390 px keeps the H/T/O columns about 100 px wide with 20 px digits; symbol tiles and number cards are large tap targets; young-mode buttons are 56 px; checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin (Hundreds/Tens/Ones, > = <, Pick then Put 1st-4th); the canvas aria-label is updated with each spoken result; walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA run in both themes.

sources: CCSS Math 2.NBT.4: compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons
